description: Agent Customs Records: submit declared-value records with the invoices and payment records they answer to: each entry with its id, entry number, the commercial invoice, the value declared and its currency, the value in the invoice currency, that currency, the exchange rate the value record states, whether a related-party purchase is declared, the valuation basis recorded and the additions to value declared (assist, royalty, packing, commission, proceeds or other); each commercial invoice with its id, reference, amount and currency; each payment to the seller with its id, the invoice, the moment paid and the amount; each addition to value the records mention with its id, the entry, its kind, the amount and where the records mention it. The signed report gives the entries and the invoices, each declared value against the amount actually paid on its invoice, each related-party purchase against its valuation basis, each addition the records mention against the additions declared, and each currency conversion recomputed from its recorded rate, and counts them, and names divergent declared-value records: a declared value that does not match the amount actually paid, a related-party purchase declared with no valuation basis recorded, an addition to value (an assist, a royalty or packing) the records mention and the declaration omits, and a currency conversion in the value record that does not recompute from the recorded rate; then a payment naming an invoice the records do not hold and an invoice paid at another amount than it states, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No entries, no payments to the seller, or an entry with no value leaves those points unverified. Entries, invoices, payments and additions match by letters and digits, the payments on one invoice add together and compare to the cent with the value the entry states in the invoice currency, and a conversion recomputes as the foreign value times the recorded rate to the cent. This reads whether the value the importer declared rests on what it actually paid. Verdict customs_valuation_divergent, customs_valuation_partial, customs_valuation_unverified or customs_valuation_consistent. POST /api/customs-valuation-check. Reads the customs and trade records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads the records as supplied only: it files no entry, pays no duty, contacts no customs authority or broker and gives no customs or legal advice, which stay with the importer, its licensed customs broker and its advisers, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Customs Records reads an importer’s or exporter’s own customs and trade records: entry summaries, tariff classification records, duty and fee payment records, broker filing records, country-of-origin and marking records, declared-value records, customs bond records and drawback claim records, each against the commercial invoices and duty payment records, the rulings on file, the entries, the importer’s own copies, the origin support on file, the invoices and payments, the entry activity or the duty recorded as paid and the proof on file. The family’s ground is the paper behind the border crossing: what was declared, how it was classified, what duty was paid, and whether the bond and the drawback claims line up; the Agent Tax Records family reads filings made to the tax authority, and the Agent Logistics family reads where a shipment is and when it moves, while this family reads neither. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-customs-records-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-customs-records/.
